name: Jacopo Tintoretto
findings: Uses raisin black 2.2x more than the other paintings from the same museum(s), so camera and varnish are held equal (from 942 paintings here).
Uses smoky black 1.8x more than the other paintings from the same museum(s), so camera and varnish are held equal (from 942 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, reed yellow turns up as a small accent in 75% of the paintings that hold it, 2.1x the archive's rate (from 942 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, mushroom brown turns up as the lightest note in 100% of the paintings that hold it, 2.4x the archive's rate (from 942 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, dim grey turns up as the shadow in 75% of the paintings that hold it, 2.4x the archive's rate (from 942 paintings here).
Pairs almond with oatmeal more than chance would predict (6 of 942 paintings here).
Pairs warm grey with zircon grey more than chance would predict (3 of 942 paintings here).
His single largest palette family (smoky black, raisin black, dark walnut) covers 61% of his paintings here.
